stem: Which finding is most characteristic of anorexia nervosa?

options.A: Recurrent loss of control while eating unusually large amounts of food, with distress about the binge episodes.
options.B: Markedly restricted food intake, intense fear of gaining weight, very low body weight, distorted body image, and denial of the seriousness of the low weight.
options.C: Recurrent binge eating followed by behaviors such as self-induced vomiting or laxative use to prevent weight gain, with weight that may remain average or higher.
options.D: Restriction of the amount or variety of food because of fear of consequences such as choking or vomiting, or because of dislike of food characteristics such as texture.

rationale: NIMH describes anorexia nervosa as severe restriction of food intake associated with intense fear of gaining weight or distorted self-image; characteristic signs include extreme thinness, distorted body image, and denial of the seriousness of low body weight. Therefore B is correct. A reflects the recurrent loss-of-control overeating pattern of binge-eating disorder. C reflects bulimia nervosa, in which binge eating is followed by behaviors such as vomiting or laxative use to prevent weight gain. D reflects ARFID, in which restriction may arise from fear of consequences such as choking or vomiting or dislike of food characteristics such as texture.
educational_objective: Recognize the characteristic cluster of anorexia nervosa: severe food restriction, intense fear of weight gain, markedly low weight, distorted body image, and poor recognition of the seriousness of low weight.
source_organization: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Eating Disorders: What You Need to Know
source_locator: What are the common types of eating disorders?; What are the signs and symptoms of anorexia nervosa?; corresponding sections for binge-eating disorder, bulimia nervosa, and avoidant restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID).
source_claim_supported: Anorexia nervosa features severe food restriction, intense fear of gaining weight, extreme thinness/low weight, distorted body image and denial of the seriousness of low weight; binge-eating disorder, bulimia nervosa and ARFID have distinct eating-behavior patterns described by NIMH.

source_original.stem: Which finding is most characteristic of anorexia nervosa?

options.A: Recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts with loss of control and distress, without compensatory behavior or a persistently low body weight.
options.B: Markedly restricted intake, intense fear of gaining weight, low body weight, distorted body image, and denial of the seriousness of low weight.
options.C: Recurrent binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting or laxative use while body weight may remain in an expected or higher range.
options.D: Restricted intake driven by food texture, sensory features, or fear of choking without a primary fear of weight gain or distorted body image.

source_original.rationale: Anorexia nervosa is characterized by severe restriction, intense fear of weight gain, low body weight, distorted body image, and often denial of the seriousness of low weight. Option B is correct. Option A better resembles binge-eating disorder. Option C describes a binge-purge pattern consistent with bulimia nervosa. Option D better resembles ARFID, where restriction is not primarily driven by weight-gain fear or distorted body image.
source_original.source_detail: NIMH — Eating Disorders: What You Need to Know, Anorexia Nervosa: severe restriction of food intake, intense fear of gaining weight/behaviors interfering with weight gain, significantly low body weight/extreme thinness, distorted body image and lack of recognition/denial of the seriousness of low weight are characteristic features. Current NIMH eating-disorders publication live-rechecked 2026-08-15; difficulty corrected to easy because the item is direct syndrome recognition with clearly differentiated eating-disorder distractors. correction_summary: Retained the stem, construct and key B. audit_findings.claim_audit: Every syndrome feature in the final options and rationale is directly represented in NIMH; no unsupported diagnostic threshold, frequency requirement or duration was added.

distractor_audit.A: Matches NIMH's binge-eating-disorder pattern of loss of control and unusually large intake, not anorexia.
distractor_audit.B: Contains the characteristic NIMH anorexia cluster.
distractor_audit.C: Matches NIMH's bulimia pattern of binge eating followed by vomiting/laxatives and possible average or higher weight.
distractor_audit.D: Matches NIMH's ARFID pattern of restriction due to feared eating consequences or disliked food characteristics.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B contains the anorexia-specific restriction/fear/low-weight/body-image cluster; the other choices map to distinct NIMH eating-disorder descriptions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are clinically coherent eating-disorder profiles of comparable complexity.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity explicitly includes care and education for eating disorders.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked NIMH wording for all four disorders, the key, rationale, objective, NCSBN locator, cueing and second-answer risk from zero; B remained uniquely best.
